entries.topicDescription: Reactive streams built on coroutines for asynchronous data processing.

tips.title: Flow basics — cold async streams
tips.content:
Flow is Kotlin's answer to reactive streams. It's cold — the producer
code runs only when someone collects the flow.

Unlike channels or LiveData, flows are declarative pipelines.
You build a flow with the 'flow { }' builder and emit values with 'emit()'.

Flows integrate naturally with coroutines — they suspend instead of blocking,
and they're cancelled when the collecting coroutine is cancelled.

tips.title: StateFlow and SharedFlow
tips.content:
StateFlow is a hot flow that always holds a current value.
It replays the latest value to new collectors and ignores duplicate emissions.

SharedFlow is more flexible — configurable replay cache and buffer.
Use it for events that shouldn't be replayed (navigation, snackbar).

StateFlow = state holder (replaces LiveData).
SharedFlow = event bus (one-shot events).
Both are hot — they exist independently of collectors.

tips.title: Flow operators — combine, flatMapLatest, debounce
tips.content:
Flow operators transform, combine, and control the timing of emissions.
They create new flows — the original flow is unchanged (immutable pipeline).

combine() merges multiple flows, emitting when any flow updates.
flatMapLatest() cancels the previous inner flow when a new value arrives.
debounce() waits for a pause in emissions before forwarding.

These operators are the building blocks of reactive UI patterns
like search-as-you-type and multi-source state combination.
